lesson.title: One High Ball. Two Opposite Answers.
lesson.hook: You retreat from every high forehand—or step into every one—and donate court.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time a ball climbs, notice its depth and your position before adjusting.

pro.label: What Swiatek chose to teach
pro.moment: For her TopCourt class, Swiatek chose drills for "handling high moon balls" and "getting in excellent court positioning".
pro.read: Champions practise the awkward ball, not just the clean one.

drill.name: In or back
drill.how: Your partner feeds high balls, some short, some deep. Call "in" or "back" before the bounce, then play it. A wrong call loses the point.

lesson.cue: Find the contact, not the height.

steps.name: A shorter high ball
steps.sit: A slower, high ball lands short. You're balanced, with time to move.
steps.q: Where do you meet this ball?
opts: Stay where you are and wait
Back up and let it drop
Move in and take it early
Move in halfway, meet it high
steps.payoff: Stepping in uses your time before the ball climbs.
steps.principle: A short high ball can be met early. Take it before it climbs.
steps.why: Waiting lets it climb above your shoulder. Backing up works, but gives them time and court. Moving in meets it at waist height.
steps.take: Short and high? Step in and take it before it climbs.

lines.A: Waiting, it's above your shoulder — you float it, they attack.
lines.B: Backing up works — waist high — but they get time and hit harder.
lines.C: Stepping in, you take it waist high — they run for it; you're in time.
lines.D: Halfway in, it's shoulder high — you float it, they attack.

steps.ph: Contrast · The early window has passed
steps.name: A deeper high ball
steps.sit: The next high ball lands deeper, while you're still getting back.
steps.q: Where do you meet this one?
opts: Back up and let it drop
Hold your ground, hit it high
Move in and take it early
steps.payoff: The early chance has gone. Back up and let it come down.
steps.principle: Same height, different answer when you arrive late.
steps.why: You can't get in early enough, so moving in meets it high. Backing up gives it time to drop to chest height.
steps.take: Late on a high ball? Back up and let it drop to chest height.

lines.A: Backing up, it drops to chest high — a deep drive; you're in time.
lines.B: Holding, it's above your shoulder — you float it, they attack.
lines.C: Sideways doesn't change depth — above your shoulder, they attack.
lines.D: Too late to take it early — it's shoulder high, they attack.

steps.name: Already well back
steps.sit: You're already well behind the baseline. The same deep ball comes.
opts: One step in, take it higher
steps.payoff: You already have the space. Stay and let it come down.
steps.principle: Read where you're standing, not just the bounce.
steps.why: From here, holding your spot meets it at chest height. Backing up further gives away court; moving in meets it higher.
steps.take: Already deep? Hold your spot — the ball comes down to you.

lines.A: Too far back — it bounces twice before you get there.
lines.B: Holding, it drops to chest high — a deep drive; you're in time.
lines.C: Moving in, it's above your shoulder — you float it, they attack.
lines.D: One step in makes it shoulder high — you loop it, only just in time.
